answer: FINAL ANSWER (concise): The RNA expression data as supplied (linear-scale values, all 20,502 genes × 328 samples pooled) are HIGHLY RIGHT-SKEWED: Fisher–Pearson skewness g1 = +42.4 on the pooled raw values (mean 932 ≫ median 177; 99.9th percentile ≈ 45,776 vs max ≈ 1,336,107), with every one of the 328 samples individually right-skewed (median per-sample g1 = +20.6, range 11.5–110.8) and 97.5% of genes right-skewed. Sensitivity context: after log2(x+1) transformation the pooled distribution becomes approximately normal with a slight left tail (g1 = −0.30; the −0.30 is driven mainly by the ~15% exact-zero values forming a left-edge spike), so the strong right skew is a property of the linear-scale data and collapses upon log-transformation.
